newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to privatise big state bank by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to privatise big state bank by year-end.

text.p: The Egyptian government will privatise in full one of the big four public-sector banks by the end of the year, a central bank official said on Wednesday.
Faika el-Rifaie, a central bank sub-governor, told Reuters the state would probably seek an investor to take 40 to 60 percent of the equity in the bank, which has not been chosen.
"It will be totally privatised and I hope that banks which are not represented now in Egypt, banks from Scandinavia, the Far East and Japan, will take this chance," she added.
The state would also offer some of the shares to the general public but it wanted an anchor investor to ensure that someone takes control of management.

Rifaie's remarks, on the sidelines of an economic conference on financial markets, was the first by an Egyptian official giving a date for privatisation of a public-sector bank and saying how big a stake the state would sell.
The four state banks, which continue to dominate the financial sector, are National Bank of Egypt (NBE), Banque Misr, Banque du Caire and Bank of Alexandria.
Business people say that NBE, the bank with the largest assets, would be the most attractive candidate because it has undergone the most radical internal modernisation.
The NBE chairman, Mahmoud Abdel-Aziz, is also the state banker most receptive to privatisation of his bank.
Shareholders' funds in NBE were worth 1.851 billion pounds ($550 million) at the end of the financial year 1995/6 and its total assets were over 50 billion pounds.
It made net profits of 130 million pounds, 30 percent up on the previous year. The years end on June 30.
It would be the biggest single privatisation since the programme began in earnest in 1993.

In the early stages of the programme, government ministers said the state banks would remain in state hands but with the recent success of privatisation they had started to drop hints that policy on this was changing.
